title: What does XLS-46 specify for Dynamic NFTs?
abstract: Sourced explanation of XLS-46 and its practical limits.
body:
According to XLS specifications, XLS-46 specifies dynamic NFTs whose URI can be updated by an authorized party. [1]

The proposal separates a stable token identifier from mutable metadata references. A URI update is an on-ledger change to a pointer; the referenced content can also depend on an external host. Buyers need to understand which party retains modification authority. Dynamic metadata does not itself transfer ownership or guarantee that an image, license or external record stays available. [1]

The public XLS-46 specification describes a design, its dependencies and its intended ledger behavior. A published standard is not proof that a feature is enabled on every XRPL network. Check the target network and any associated fixes before relying on the capability. Testnet, Mainnet and development networks can support different amendment sets, and examples in a proposal are explanatory rather than records of validated transactions. [1][2]

The fetched specification records its status as Final. [1] Author interpretation: compare the proposed use of XLS-46 with the actual network capability and preserve the resulting evidence. Keep a design reference separate from a deployment claim and from a successful transaction receipt. This article makes no fresh network-activation claim. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
